newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crudes ease, refiners sidelined.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crudes ease, refiners sidelined.

text.p: U.S West Coast light crudes tracked falling prices for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Monday, while discounts stayed flat as refiners figured out their production for next month, traders said.
The major seller of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude declined to offer a price for the grade, drying up Monday discussion, traders said.

Company traders said they were assessing their next move after two deals late last week sent ANS prices to their highest relative price since early 1996. Some buyers feared a repeat of a $0.60 cents discount seen this time a year-ago.
ANS outright prices fell five cents from Friday to $19.25/19.45 a barrel.
Line 63 prices stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05, with the market quiet ahead of Tuesday's auction for Elk Hills crudes, key components of blended Line 63.
Kern River heavy crude prices fell, after a major California oil company lowered postings Monday.
The last heavy deal was heard done last week at 0.45 cents a barrel under heavy postings, but no deals were heard Monday.
